articles.title: Behind the Label Lies a Longer and Stranger Chemical Story
articles.summary: A new review of textile chemistry challenges the assumption that natural fibers are always more environmentally friendly than synthetics. The study finds that the environmental impact of clothing depends more on dyes, finishes, and treatments used throughout production, use, and disposal than on the fiber type itself. This raises concerns about chemical pollution and sustainability in India's textile industry, which is a major sector for the country.
articles.raw_summary: Many consumers assume that natural fibres are automatically kinder to the environment than synthetic alternatives. A new systematic review of textile chemistry complicates this rule of thumb, showing that the environmental cost of a garment depends less on fibre origin than on the dyes, finishes and performance treatments applied throughout production, wear, disposal and recycling stages.

articles.title: Energy sector in spotlight as cyberattack threat grows
articles.summary: The energy sector in India faces increasing cyberattack risks as information technology (IT) and operational technology (OT) systems converge due to rapid modernization. Historically separate networks are now integrated, creating complex cyber-physical systems that are harder to secure. Energy companies are modernizing their networks to improve service delivery, but this shift raises significant cybersecurity challenges that could impact national infrastructure.
articles.raw_summary: The age of convergence describes the rapid connectivity in recent years as information and operational technology have come together in unprecedented ways. These two environments were historically kept separate, but as energy companies have rapidly modernised their networks to improve service delivery, these two worlds have converged. The result is complex cyber-physical systems that are difficult to secure.

articles.title: Facebook, TikTok promoted Colombian armed groups' content to recruit children: NGO
articles.summary: Human Rights Watch (HRW) reported that Facebook and TikTok promoted content by Colombian armed groups that glorifies life in their ranks and uses deceptive job offers to recruit children. Since 2021, around 1,500 children have been recruited by these groups. The NGO highlighted the role of social media in facilitating such recruitment, raising concerns about platform accountability and child protection.

articles.summary: The Indian government has rejected requests from bulk sugar users for more time to sell excess stocks, requiring them to liquidate surplus by August 31. articles.title: As obesity rises, Supreme Court puts govt on notice over junk food labels
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has issued a notice to the central government over its reluctance to implement front-of-pack warning labels on junk food. The order follows a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) filed by the NGO '3S and Our HEALTH Society' through advocate Rajiv Shankar Dvivedi. The court emphasized that high salt, sugar, saturated fat, and calorie content in such foods poses health risks and stressed the need for clearer nutrition information to help consumers make healthier choices.
